column1: # Closed lists that stay closed: file, name, reason class, expert way out (tab-separated).
# Reason classes: grammar, soundness, ir, kernel, protocol, fixed-standard.

column4: the musl thread functions the C startup builds the runtime's thread functions from (link_thread_create's pthread_attr_init, pthread_attr_setstacksize, pthread_create and pthread_attr_destroy, then pthread_join and pthread_detach as they are), handed to JetRuntime Thread.jet jet_rt_thread_libc in three fixed argument registers; another function is a new call in that synthesized code or a new parameter of that export, and library code starts threads through the runtime's thread_spawn instead
the x86-64 ALU opcode group the encoder emits, fixed by the instruction set; another instruction is a new variant with its encoding, not a library extension
the sixteen x86-64 condition codes, fixed by the instruction set; there is nothing for library code to extend
the x86-64 shift group the encoder emits, fixed by the instruction set; another shift is a new variant with its encoding, not a library extension

the row kinds of the x86-64 emission log (JET_X64_EMIT_LOG), one per instruction form the encoder writes that can branch or touch memory (jcc, jmp, call, call through a register, memory operand, division, string copy, inline-asm template); a new form is a new variant the encoder logs, not a library extension

the sixteen x86-64 general-purpose register names by encoding number (rax through r15), as the emission log prints a row's base and index registers; fixed by the instruction set, there is nothing for library code to extend

the sixteen x86-64 condition-code mnemonics by condition number (o through g), as the emission log prints a jcc row; fixed by the instruction set like X64Cond, there is nothing for library code to extend

the runtime's fiber context switch, the one template whose saved-register layout every switch site shares so any site resumes any other, assembled only to X64_FIBER_SWITCH_BYTES and only for the runtime library that defines the fiber entry; another rail is a new constant with its fixed bytes and its arm in x64_assemble_template, and library code switches fibers through the runtime's scheduler instead

the whole body of a signal restorer: rt_sigreturn (syscall 15) on the stack the handler returned to, fixed by the Linux x86-64 signal frame ABI and assembled only to X64_SIGNAL_RETURN_BYTES for the runtime library; there is nothing for library code to extend, and code installs handlers through the runtime's signal routes instead

the entry-based `jet audit` subcommands (copies, foreign, writes), each a command word the CLI parses into its own report plan; another subject is a new `jet audit` subcommand with its plan and report, not a library extension

the exact field set of an accepted generation's audit record in the `jet.budget-manifest` schema; another field is a new manifest schema version that the store writes and reads together, not a library extension

the budget report measurement fields a prior baseline generation must share with the candidate to be compared with it; another field changes which stored reports compare, so it lands with a budget report schema version
the budget report subject fields (target triple, target class, profile) a prior baseline generation must share with the candidate; another field lands with a budget report schema version

the three ways `jet budget update` accepts a report, each written as the audit `kind` (`pass`, `bootstrap`, `exception`) the manifest reader checks; another way is a new audit kind in the manifest schema

the three states the baseline staleness rule gives a budget's newest compatible generation (none, fresh, stale), which decide whether a bootstrap may replace it; another state is a change to that rule, not a library extension

the four kinds of node the `jet build` scheduler runs (a step, a target's image, a checked library, a target built for the machine running the build), each with its own arm that starts and finishes it; another kind is a new Build call with its scheduler arm, not a library extension, and library code adds work to a build as a `b.run` step
the artifact file kinds Jet writes, each paired with its fixed extension in ARTIFACT_KINDS; another kind is a new artifact format with its own extension and reader, not a library extension
the argument shapes an interpolation format selector takes in its parentheses; another shape is a change to the interpolation grammar through the syntax registry
the token classes the highlight generator assigns every grammar token for the editor grammars it writes; another class is a change to the generated grammars, not a library extension
the binary operators the grammar parses; a new operator is a language change through the syntax registry, and library code names an operation as a function instead

the ways a `jet` flag is written on the command line (bare, bare or `=false`, one value, bare or one value, one value per repeat), each with its own arm where a remembered setting writes the flag's words; another way is a change to the command-line grammar, not a library extension

the four kinds of row in the public metadata contract (fact, operation, phase, failure), the classes #3520's versioned model publishes and Tests/MetadataContract.jet checks every row against; another kind is a new version of that contract on #3520, not a library extension

the four surfaces of the public metadata contract (preparation, reflection, publishing, advanced program control), the parts #3520's versioned model is cut into and Tests/MetadataContract.jet checks every row against; another surface is a new version of that contract on #3520, not a library extension
the IR instruction set every backend lowers; library code reaches new behavior through Core calls and runtime routes, and a new op lands with its lowering in every backend

the share keys the IR builder emits as the clone of a counted value (a box, a trait value, a function value), each lowered by every backend as a retain; a new counted kind lands with its clone lowering and its row here, not as a library extension

the semantic-token legend `initialize` announces; a token's type travels as its index here (LSP_TOKEN_* in Tokens.jet), so another type is a new LSP_TOKEN_* constant and legend entry the client reads together, not a library extension

the exceptions of the impl placement style rule (#6561 rules c, d, e, f and g: a protocol side, a `#Target` impl, a derive-written impl, an impl whose head carries an error of the same check, an inherent impl with its own markers; #6281 c159 rule h: a conditional impl, whose head bounds its type's parameters), each an impl form, marker or head error the grammar gives that the type's body cannot hold as written, with its own arm in parser_impl_placement_rule, which `jet check --style`, `jet fix --style` and the impl placement guard share; another exception is a change to that rule on #6561, not a library extension

the lexer files Toolchain/LexerKeywordRows.jet projects the keyword spans from, the lexer-keywords step's declared inputs; another file lands with that generator and this row, not as a library extension
the compiler sources Toolchain/PreludeSources.jet writes from the Prelude, the prelude-sources step's kept outputs; another copy lands with that generator and this row, not as a library extension

the Prelude files Toolchain/PreludeSources.jet carries into the compiler, the prelude-sources step's declared inputs; another file is a Prelude layout change that lands with that generator and this row, not a library extension

the files of the runtime pack beside jet, which Toolchain/RuntimePack.jet writes and jet's native link reads, each a declared output of the runtime step; another file is a pack layout change that lands with RuntimePack.jet and its reader, not a library extension

the Compiler folders whose sources make the runtime pack (the runtime and its IR, x86-64 and WebAssembly producer), mounted into the runtime step and hashed into native.key; another folder is a repository layout change that lands with this row, not a library extension

the optimize levels the core suite runs each Core #Test at, one `jet test <file> --optimize=<level>` each: a copy of the `optimize` row's values in Compiler/JetFoundation/Source/Registry/BuildOptions.jet, which test.jet (a script that imports only Core) can't read; closed_lists.jet fails when the two differ, so another level lands in that row and here together, not as a library extension
the checkout trees (AGENTS.md repository layout) whose #Tests the coverage row requires some suite to run; another tree is a repository layout change that lands with this row, not a library extension
the checkout trees (AGENTS.md repository layout) whose packages the packages suite runs; another tree is a repository layout change that lands with this row, not a library extension

the trees under tests/ whose .jet files are another suite's inputs (cases, workloads, snapshots, goldens, witnesses, fuzz corpora), so their #Test text is input rather than a test some package owes a run; another tree is a test-suite layout change that lands with this row, not a library extension

the four operations of mbedtls 3.6.7's CCM layer (ccm.h MBEDTLS_CCM_ENCRYPT, MBEDTLS_CCM_DECRYPT, MBEDTLS_CCM_STAR_ENCRYPT, MBEDTLS_CCM_STAR_DECRYPT): CCM (NIST SP 800-38C) and CCM* (IEEE 802.15.4) in each direction; another mode is a new block-cipher mode with its own construction, not a library extension

the MBEDTLS_ERR_ASN1_* failure codes of mbedtls 3.6.7's asn1.h (out of data, unexpected tag, invalid length, length mismatch, invalid data, buffer too small), the code a sequence visitor stops with, and the MPI failure they wrap, which the asn1parse and asn1write vectors check one to one; another failure is a new code raised by core.crypto's ASN.1 layer, not a library extension, and programs report their own errors in their own types

the MBEDTLS_ERR_MPI_* failure codes of mbedtls 3.6.7's bignum.h, one variant per code, which the test_suite_bignum vectors check one to one; another failure is a new code raised by core.crypto's MPI layer, not a library extension, and programs report their own errors in their own types

the five CBC padding schemes of mbedtls 3.6.7's cipher layer (cipher.h mbedtls_cipher_padding_t: PKCS7, ONE_AND_ZEROS, ZEROS_AND_LEN, ZEROS, NONE), each with the add and check routines the test_suite_cipher padding vectors pin; another scheme is a new padding construction with its own routines, not a library extension

the keyed contexts of mbedtls 3.6.7's cipher_wrap.c bases (AES, AES-XTS, DES and Triple-DES, Camellia, ARIA, GCM and CCM over each 128-bit cipher, ChaCha20, ChaCha20-Poly1305, the AES key wrap) that a cipher-layer context runs on; another variant is a new cipher with its own primitive, not a library extension

mbedtls 3.6.7's mbedtls_cipher_id_t (NULL, AES, DES, 3DES, CAMELLIA, ARIA, CHACHA20), the cipher families the cipher layer's table rows name; another family is a new block or stream cipher with its own primitive, not a library extension

the MBEDTLS_ERR_CIPHER_* failure codes of mbedtls 3.6.7's cipher.h and the AES, GCM, CCM, ChaCha20 and ChaCha20-Poly1305 codes the cipher layer passes through, which the test_suite_cipher vectors check one to one; another failure is a new code raised by core.crypto's cipher layer, not a library extension, and programs report their own errors in their own types

mbedtls 3.6.7's mbedtls_cipher_mode_t (ECB, CBC, CFB, OFB, CTR, GCM, STREAM, CCM, CCM_STAR_NO_TAG, XTS, CHACHAPOLY, KW, KWP), the modes of operation of NIST SP 800-38A, 38C, 38D, 38E and 38F, RFC 8439 and IEEE 802.15.4 that the cipher layer dispatches on; another mode is a new construction with its own routines, not a library extension

the MBEDTLS_ERR_DHM_* failure codes of mbedtls 3.6.7's dhm.h with the MPI, ASN.1 or PEM failure they wrap, which the test_suite_dhm vectors check one to one; another failure is a new code raised by core.crypto's DHM layer, not a library extension, and programs report their own errors in their own types
mbedtls 3.6.7's mbedtls_dhm_parameter (P, G, X, GX, GY, K), the Diffie-Hellman values of RFC 2631 that mbedtls_dhm_get_value reads; another value is a change to the exchange, not a library extension

the MBEDTLS_ERR_CTR_DRBG_* and MBEDTLS_ERR_HMAC_DRBG_* failure codes of mbedtls 3.6.7 (entropy source failed, request too big, input too big, file I/O), which the DRBG suite vectors check; another failure is a new code raised by core.crypto's DRBG layer, not a library extension
mbedtls 3.6.7's mbedtls_ecp_curve_type (none, short Weierstrass, Montgomery), the curve shapes the ECP arithmetic implements; another shape is new point arithmetic, not a library extension

the MBEDTLS_ERR_ECP_* failure codes of mbedtls 3.6.7's ecp.h plus the MPI failure they wrap, which the test_suite_ecp vectors check one to one; another failure is a new code raised by core.crypto's ECP layer, not a library extension, and programs report their own errors in their own types

the fast modular reductions of mbedtls 3.6.7's ecp_curves.c (the NIST primes P-192 to P-521, Curve25519's and Curve448's primes, the secp-k1 primes) and the generic Montgomery path, chosen per curve by the group table; another reduction lands with the curve that needs it, not as a library extension

mbedtls 3.6.7's mbedtls_ecp_group_id: the named curves of SEC 2, RFC 5639 and RFC 7748 that the ECP layer carries domain parameters for, numbered as the TLS Supported Groups registry maps them; another curve is new domain parameters and arithmetic, not a library extension

the failures mbedtls 3.6.7's LMS layer returns (MBEDTLS_ERR_LMS_BAD_INPUT_DATA, OUT_OF_PRIVATE_KEYS, VERIFY_FAILED, and a failed random source), which the test_suite_lms vectors check; another failure is a new code raised by core.crypto's LMS layer, not a library extension

the message digests of mbedtls 3.6.7's md.h (MD5, RIPEMD-160, SHA-1 and SHA-2 of FIPS 180-4, SHA-3 of FIPS 202), each with its compression function in this file; another digest is a new variant with its compression function, not a library extension

mbedtls 3.6.7's mbedtls_pk_type_t as the OID tables map it (RSA, EC key, ECDH-only key, ECDSA, RSA-alt, RSASSA-PSS, opaque), the public key algorithms of RFC 3279, RFC 4055 and RFC 5480; another key type is a new algorithm with its OIDs, not a library extension
the RFC 1421 DEK-Info algorithms mbedtls 3.6.7's pem.c decrypts (DES-EDE3-CBC, DES-CBC, AES-128-CBC, AES-192-CBC, AES-256-CBC); another algorithm is a new DEK-Info decryption, not a library extension

the MBEDTLS_ERR_PEM_* failure codes of mbedtls 3.6.7's pem.h with the Base64 or DES failure they wrap, which the test_suite_pem vectors check one to one; another failure is a new code raised by core.crypto's PEM layer, not a library extension, and programs report their own errors in their own types

the MBEDTLS_ERR_PK_* failure codes of mbedtls 3.6.7's pk.h with the ASN.1 or EC failure they add, plus the RSA, EC, ECDSA, ASN.1, OID, PEM, PKCS #5 and PKCS #12 failures pk.c, pkparse.c and pkwrite.c pass on unchanged, which the test_suite_pk, test_suite_pkparse and test_suite_pkwrite vectors check one to one; another failure is a new code raised by core.crypto's public-key layer, not a library extension, and programs report their own errors in their own types

the four failure codes that mbedtls 3.6.7's pkcs5.h (MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS5_*) and pkcs12.h (MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS12_*) share (bad input data, invalid format, feature unavailable, password mismatch), with the ASN.1 or cipher-layer failure they wrap, which the test_suite_pkcs5 and test_suite_pkcs12 vectors check one to one; another failure is a new code raised by core.crypto's password-based encryption, not a library extension, and programs report their own errors in their own types

the MBEDTLS_ERR_PKCS7_* failure codes of mbedtls 3.6.7's pkcs7.h that pkcs7.c returns, with the ASN.1 failure they add, plus the ASN.1, OID and public-key failures pkcs7.c passes on unchanged, which the test_suite_pkcs7 vectors check one to one; another failure is a new code raised by core.crypto's PKCS #7 layer, not a library extension, and programs report their own errors in their own types

the MBEDTLS_ERR_RSA_* failure codes of mbedtls 3.6.7's rsa.h with the MPI or ASN.1 failure they wrap, which the test_suite_rsa vectors check one to one; another failure is a new code raised by core.crypto's RSA layer, not a library extension, and programs report their own errors in their own types

the RSA key components N, P, Q, D and E of PKCS #1 (RFC 8017 section 3) that mbedtls_rsa_import and mbedtls_rsa_export take one by one; another component is a change to the key format, not a library extension

the six GeneralName forms of RFC 5280 section 4.2.1.6 that mbedtls 3.6.7's mbedtls_x509_parse_subject_alt_name reads (otherName with a hardwareModuleName, rfc822Name, dNSName, directoryName, uniformResourceIdentifier, iPAddress), each with the content mbedtls keeps; any other form is FeatureUnavailable as in mbedtls, and another form is a new parse in core.crypto's X.509 layer, not a library extension

the MBEDTLS_ERR_X509_* failure codes of mbedtls 3.6.7's x509.h with the ASN.1 or OID failure they add, plus the ASN.1, OID, public-key and PEM failures x509.c, x509_crt.c, x509_crl.c, x509_csr.c, x509_create.c, x509write.c, x509write_crt.c and x509write_csr.c pass on unchanged and the code of its own a verification callback fails with, which the test_suite_x509parse and test_suite_x509write vectors check one to one; another failure is a new code raised by core.crypto's X.509 layer, not a library extension, and programs report their own errors in their own types

the texts of mbedtls 3.6.7's X509_CRT_ERROR_INFO list, one per MBEDTLS_X509_BADCERT_* and MBEDTLS_X509_BADCRL_* verification flag in bit order, which mbedtls_x509_crt_verify_info prints and the test_suite_x509parse verify_info vectors check byte for byte; another text comes with a new flag in x509.h, not a library extension

the operand kinds a VdbeOp's P4 holds in SQLite 3.45.0 (vdbe.h P4_NOTUSED, P4_TRANSIENT/STATIC/DYNAMIC text, P4_COLLSEQ, P4_INT32, P4_INT64, P4_REAL, P4_SUBPROGRAM, P4_TABLE, P4_TABLEREF, P4_FUNCDEF, P4_FUNCCTX, P4_KEYINFO, P4_MEM, P4_VTAB, P4_INTARRAY, P4_EXPR), which the ported opcodes and EXPLAIN's P4 column read one to one; another kind comes with a new opcode of a later SQLite release, not a library extension

the compile options SQLite 3.45.0's sqlite3azCompileOpt (ctime.c) lists for the build Core/Db ships, sorted A-Z, which sqlite3_compileoption_get and sqlite3_compileoption_used read; another option is a different build of the library, not a library extension

the result column names SQLite 3.45.0 gives PRAGMA table_info (cid, name, type, notnull, dflt_value, pk) and table_xinfo (those and hidden), pragCName[8..14] in pragma.h; programs read these columns by position or by these names, so there is nothing for library code to extend

the EXPLAIN name of each of SQLite 3.45.0's 190 VDBE opcodes, in the sqlite3.c amalgamation's opcode order (opcodes.c), which EXPLAIN's opcode column prints; another opcode is a new SQLite release with its own numbering, not a library extension

the result column names SQLite 3.45.0 gives EXPLAIN (addr, opcode, p1, p2, p3, p4, p5, comment) and EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN (id, parent, notused, detail) in vdbeapi.c columnName; programs read these columns by position or by these names, so there is nothing for library code to extend

the six access patterns posix_fadvise and madvise take (normal, sequential, random, will-need, don't-need, read-once), fixed by POSIX and Linux; another pattern is a new kernel advice value with its code in advice_code, not a library extension, and code that needs another hint reads and caches the file itself

the three ways the strict application/x-www-form-urlencoded decode of the WHATWG URL standard refuses input (a % not followed by two hex digits, decoded bytes that are not UTF-8, input above the 1 MiB body cap), each one point where the tolerant decode of that standard keeps the input instead; another refusal is a change to the strict decode, not a library extension, and code that refuses more input checks the decoded Query itself

the six core.log levels, lowest first (debug, info, warn, error, critical, fatal), the ratified fixed ladder whose names the `level` and `module=level` pairs of JET_LOG, `--log` and the package `log:` field spell and every JSON record writes; another level is a change to that filter syntax and record schema, not a library extension, and library code tells records apart with fields

the five directions C23's fromfp family rounds to an integer in (FP_INT_UPWARD, FP_INT_DOWNWARD, FP_INT_TOWARDZERO, FP_INT_TONEARESTFROMZERO, FP_INT_TONEAREST), which round_to_signed and round_to_unsigned take; another direction is a change to that standard, and code that needs another rounding rounds the Float itself before converting

mbedtls 3.6.7's mbedtls_key_exchange_type_t as the default configuration builds it (none, RSA, DHE-RSA, ECDHE-RSA, ECDHE-ECDSA, PSK, DHE-PSK, RSA-PSK, ECDHE-PSK, ECDH-RSA, ECDH-ECDSA; EC J-PAKE is off), the TLS 1.2 key exchanges of RFC 5246, 4279, 5489 and 8422 that each ciphersuite row names; another exchange is a new ciphersuite family with its handshake messages, not a library extension

the MBEDTLS_ERR_SSL_* failure codes of mbedtls 3.6.7's ssl.h, one variant per code, plus MBEDTLS_ERR_ERROR_CORRUPTION_DETECTED, MBEDTLS_ERR_ERROR_GENERIC_ERROR, a failed random source, a callback's own code, and the cipher, public-key, X.509, ECP, DHM and MPI failures mbedtls returns unchanged from the layers under the TLS engine; another failure is a new code raised by the engine, not a library extension

mbedtls 3.6.7's mbedtls_ssl_mode_t as the default configuration builds it (stream, CBC, CBC with encrypt-then-MAC of RFC 7366, AEAD; the NULL cipher is off), the ways a TLS record is protected; another mode is a new record protection in encrypt_buf and decrypt_buf, not a library extension

the three phases a Jet program's code evaluates in (Preparation inside comptime, Build in a package build, Runtime in the running program), which `#phase` reads at the evaluation site; the compiler fixes the phase of every expression, so another phase is a new evaluation stage in the compiler, not a library extension

the three forms a POSIX TZ rule's transition date takes (POSIX.1-2017 Base Definitions section 8.3, TZ): Jn, the Julian day 1 to 365 that never counts February 29; n, the zero-based day 0 to 365 that does; Mm.w.d, day d of week w of month m; as a TZif version 2+ footer carries them (RFC 8536 section 3.3); another form is a change to that standard, not a library extension, and code that needs another rule computes its own offsets from the zone's transitions

the ways core.ui's private D-Bus client fails (no session bus, the socket, the authentication, a protocol break, a closed bus, a timeout, an error reply), each raised by that client; it is compiler-private and core.ui turns it into its own defaults, so another failure is a new variant raised there, not a library extension

the D-Bus specification's value types (byte, boolean, the six integers, double, string, object path, signature, variant, array, struct, dict entry), one variant per type code; Unix descriptors (`h`) are not negotiated and so have none, and another type is a change to that specification, not a library extension

the D-Bus specification's four message types (method call, method return, error, signal) by their wire codes 1 to 4; a message of another code is skipped as the specification says, and another type is a change to that specification

the values of the XDG desktop portal's org.freedesktop.appearance color-scheme setting (0 no preference, 1 prefer dark, 2 prefer light), with any other value read as no preference as the portal documents; another scheme is a change to that interface

the title-bar buttons Jet's own window frame draws (minimize, maximize, close, or none under the pointer or holding the keyboard focus), each mapped by the Wayland part to one xdg_toplevel request; the frame is compiler-private and programs never name it, so another button is a new variant drawn and wired by core.ui's frame, not a library extension

the parts of a window Jet's own frame tells apart under the pointer (outside, content, title bar, a button, a resize edge), each mapped by the Wayland part to one xdg_toplevel request or to the program's own input; the frame is compiler-private, so another part is a new variant with its arm in that mapping, not a library extension

the ways the window layer itself fails (no display, the connection, the display server's protocol, a missing protocol feature, a wrong pixel size, a malformed app_id or icon name), each produced by the backend that core.ui owns; a new failure is a new variant raised by that backend, and programs report their own errors in their own types
the Linux evdev pointer buttons BTN_LEFT, BTN_RIGHT and BTN_MIDDLE by name, with every other button code carried by `Other(Int)`; there is nothing for library code to extend

the CSS cursor keywords in the order the wp_cursor_shape_v1 protocol numbers its shapes, plus `Hidden` for CSS `none`; another shape is a new protocol version's, not a library extension, and a program's own cursor image is a separate feature

the input a window delivers to a frame, each variant produced by one dispatch arm of each backend core.ui owns; a new kind of input is a new variant with its arm in every backend, and programs build their own event types from these

the unshifted symbols of the US ANSI keyboard rows in Linux evdev key code order, the fallback when the compositor sends no keymap; there is nothing for library code to extend, and a layout comes from the compositor's XKB keymap instead

the shifted symbols of the US ANSI keyboard rows in Linux evdev key code order, the fallback when the compositor sends no keymap; there is nothing for library code to extend, and a layout comes from the compositor's XKB keymap instead

the MIME types Wayland and X11 clients exchange plain text under (text/plain;charset=utf-8, UTF8_STRING, text/plain, TEXT, STRING), preferred first: a paste takes the first one the other client offers and a copy offers them all; another type is another clipboard format, which core.ui would read with its own decoder, not a library extension

the five Linux scheduling policies sched_setscheduler takes (SCHED_OTHER, SCHED_BATCH, SCHED_IDLE, and SCHED_FIFO and SCHED_RR with their static priority), fixed by POSIX and Linux; another policy (SCHED_DEADLINE, set through sched_setattr with its own runtime, deadline and period) is a new variant with its kernel number and arguments, not a library extension

the packages whose `use <package>` lines the assembled Jetpack unit blanks, because the unit is one namespace; another package joins the unit through Jetpack/Bootstrap/sources.list and lands with its row here, not as a library extension

the only names a `project` directory may hold if the assembly is to remove it before writing it again: `src` and `package.jet`, which the assembly writes, and `.jet`, which `jet check` and `jet build` make beside the manifest; project_removal_refusal refuses any directory that holds another name, so a scratch variable that is stale or empty can never make the recursive remove reach a checkout or HOME; another name is a new file that the assembly or its jet run writes into the project, and it lands with that write and its row here, not as a library extension

the three things publishing a declared output does to the file under the project root (write the made bytes, leave a kept output that already holds them, refuse a kept output edited by hand), each with its own arm in the cache restore and the executor's publish; another outcome is a change to the kept-output rule, not a library extension

the library folders a find_folder probe searches after LIBRARY_PATH: the Filesystem Hierarchy Standard's /usr/local/lib, /usr/lib and /lib, then the two a musl install puts libc.a in (a distribution's /usr/lib/musl/lib, musl's own default prefix /usr/local/musl/lib); another folder changes the probe's search order, and a machine with libraries elsewhere names them on LIBRARY_PATH

the three ways the native sandbox itself fails a child (no enforcing backend, an I/O failure, the time limit), which the build executor maps to its own reports; another failure the sandbox detects lands with its message and that mapping, and code that wraps the sandbox reports its own error type instead

the compiler operations library code inside the compiler may perform (checked generation, including outside source, replacing a body, advanced types, declarations from text), each checked by the compiler against the caller's row; reading the program needs none, so a library that only reads declares no case, and another operation lands with the compiler code that checks it
